Real numbers: geometric representation of real numbers, interval, absolute value

card.title: Sequence and series: arithmetic, geometric, harmonic sequences

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A sequence is an ordered list a1, a2, a3, ... following a pattern, and a series is the sum of its terms. In an arithmetic progression the difference d = a_n - a_(n-1) is constant, giving a_n = a + (n-1)d and S_n = n/2[2a + (n-1)d] = n/2(a + l); in a geometric progression the ratio r = a_n/a_(n-1) is constant, giving a_n = a r^(n-1) and S_n = a(r^n - 1)/(r - 1), which reduces to a/(1 - r) only when |r| < 1.…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: x HP has a direct sum formula. x Take reciprocals, use AP sum.  ·  x r can be any value in infinite GP. x Must have |r| < 1 for convergence.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: A harmonic progression has no sum formula of its own: take reciprocals, sum the resulting AP, and the sum of the HP is the sum of the reciprocals of those partial sums.  ·  If r = 1 the GP is constant with S_n = na, and the formula carrying (r - 1) in the denominator is undefined.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Find the 20th term and sum of first 20 terms of AP: 3, 7, 11, ...  ·  Find the GP: 2, 6, 18, ... and its 8th term.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: x AM = GM always. x AM >= GM, equality only when all terms equal.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Find the nth term and the sum of the first n terms of a given AP, having first identified a and d, or the last term l, from the listed terms.  ·  Find the nth term and the sum to n terms of a GP, having first identified the common ratio by dividing any term by the one before it.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Read the first three terms: a constant second difference means AP, while a constant ratio means GP.  ·  For the sum of n terms of an AP use S_n = n/2(a + l) when the last term is given, and n/2[2a + (n-1)d] otherwise.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Find the 20th term and the sum of the first 20 terms of the AP 3, 7, 11, ...  ·  Find the common ratio and the 8th term of the GP 2, 6, 18, ..., and state the formula for S_n.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: MCQs ask for a single missing term, the common difference or ratio, or the nature of a given series, all in about 1 mark.  ·  5-mark questions typically ask for the nth term and S_n of an AP or a GP, and 10-mark questions add an infinite sum or a word problem.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Arithmetic progression: the successive differences a_n - a_(n-1) = d are constant, so terms rise by equal jumps.  ·  Geometric progression: the successive ratios a_n/a_(n-1) = r are constant, so each term is a fixed multiple of the previous one.  ·  Harmonic progression: the reciprocals 1/a, 1/(a+d), 1/(a+2d) form an arithmetic progression, so it has no direct sum formula.  ·  Means of two positive numbers a and b: A = (a+b)/2, G = sqrt(ab) and H = 2ab/(a+b), with A >= G >= H.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: A difference signals an AP and a ratio signals a GP, so subtract a(n-1) to get d and divide by a(n-1) to get r.  ·  S_n = n/2(a + l) is often the quickest AP sum, because l is usually given directly in the question.  ·  For a GP with r < 1, write S_n as a(1 - r^n)/(1 - r) so that the bracket stays positive.  ·  Never use S_infinity = a/(1 - r) without first confirming that |r| < 1.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: If the AM of two positive numbers is 13 and their GM is 12, find the two numbers.  ·  Find the sum to infinity of 1 + 1/3 + 1/9 + ... and state the condition on the common ratio.  ·  The first term of a GP is 5 and the sum to infinity is 10; find the common ratio and hence the third term.

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Word problems on salary, instalments or interest are AP and GP wordings, so convert them to a_n = a + (n-1)d or a_n = a r^(n-1) before any algebra.  ·  The chain A >= G >= H is a frequent 1-mark MCQ, and recovering the two numbers from A and H is a standard 5-mark question.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: The 20th term of the AP 3, 7, 11, ... is → B  ·  The sum to infinity of the series 1 + 1/3 + 1/9 + ... is → A

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ### 1. Sequence Definition  ·  An ordered list of numbers following a pattern: a1, a2, a3, ..., an, ...  ·  ### 2. Arithmetic Progression (AP)

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: An infinite GP converges to a/(1 - r) only when |r| < 1; for r = 1 the terms stay constant and for r > 1 they grow.  ·  The last term l of an AP is l = a + (n-1)d, which lets S_n be written in the short form n/2(a + l).  ·  Sn = a(r^n - 1)/(r-1) (GP)

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: S_infinity = a/(1-r), |r| < 1 (GP)  ·  G = sqrt(ab), H = 2ab/(a+b)  ·  AM, GM and HM are means of two numbers; they are not obtained by averaging the terms of a progression.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Negative or zero r still give a valid finite sum formula, but the series diverges to infinity unless |r| < 1.  ·  AM = GM = HM only when every number is equal, so a strict inequality A > G > H is the signal that the numbers are not identical.  ·  Arithmetic mean is always defined, but GM needs non-negative numbers and HM needs non-zero numbers, since the means are taken over reciprocals.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The nth term of an AP with first term a and common difference d is a_n = a + (n-1)d, and the sum of n terms is S_n = n/2[2a + (n-1)d] = n/2(a + l).  ·  The nth term of a GP with first term a and common ratio r is a_n = a r^(n-1), and for r != 1 the sum of n terms is S_n = a(r^n - 1)/(r - 1).  ·  An infinite geometric series 1 + r + r^2 + ... sums to S_infinity = a/(1 - r) if and only if |r| < 1.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: For two positive numbers the geometric mean is G = sqrt(ab) and the harmonic mean is H = 2ab/(a+b), and these satisfy A x H = G^2.  ·  For positive numbers AM >= GM >= HM, with equality in any of the three comparisons only when a = b.  ·  To find two numbers from their AM and GM, set x + y = 2A and xy = G^2, then solve t^2 - 2At + G^2 = 0.
